'''Anne Geneviève L'Huillier''' ({{IPA|fr|an lɥije|lang}}; born 16 August 1958)<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Nobel Prize in Physics 2023 |url=https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2023/lhuillier/facts/ |access-date=4 October 2023 |website=NobelPrize.org |language=en-US}}</ref> is a French [[physicist]].<ref name=":2" /> She is a professor of [[atomic physics]] at [[Lund University]] in Sweden.  

She leads an [[Attophysics|attosecond physics]] group which works through the movements of [[electron]]s in real time, which is used to understand chemical reactions on the atomic level.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Carl Zeiss Research Award |url=https://www.zeiss.com/corporate/int/innovation-and-technology/research-award-winners.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170219003440/https://www.zeiss.com/corporate/int/innovation-and-technology/research-award-winners.html |archive-date=19 February 2017 |access-date=29 April 2017 |website=ZEISS International |language=en}}</ref> 
Her [[experimental physics|experimental]] and [[theoretical physics|theoretical]] research are credited with laying the foundation for the field of attochemistry.<ref name="Bubola">{{cite news |last1=Bubola |first1=Emma |last2=Miller |first2=Katrina |title=Nobel Prize in Physics Awarded to 3 Scientists for Illuminating How Electrons Move |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/10/03/science/nobel-prize-physics.html |work=The New York Times |date=3 October 2023}}</ref>
In 2003 she and her group beat the world record for the shortest laser pulse, of 170 [[attosecond]]s.<ref name="Fysik"/> 

L'Huillier became a member of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]] in 2004.<ref name=":2"/> She has received various physics awards including the [[Wolf Prize in Physics]] in 2022<ref name=":3" /> and the [[Nobel Prize in Physics]] in 2023.<ref name="davis-2023">
{{cite news
 | last1 = Davis | first1 = Nicola
 | title = Nobel prize in physics awarded to three scientists for work on electrons
 | date = 3 October 2023
| work = The Guardian
 | location = London, United Kingdom
 | issn = 0261-3077
 | url = https://www.theguardian.com/science/2023/oct/03/nobel-prize-in-physics-awarded-to-three-scientists-for-work-on-electrons
 | access-date = 3 October 2023
}}
</ref> In 2024 she was awarded the Great Gold Medal of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Engineering Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=IVA's Great Gold Medal 2024: Anne L'Huillier – opened the door to the world of atoms |url=https://www.iva.se/en/published/ivas-great-gold-medal-2024-anne-lhuillier--opened-the-door-to-the-world-of-atoms/ |access-date=2026-11-07 |website=www.iva.se |language=en}}</ref>

== Life ==

=== Education ===
Anne L'Huillier was born in [[Paris]] in 1958.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Anne L'Huillier |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/anne-lhuillier-uaulae/ |access-date=3 October 2023 |website=National Academy of Sciences}}</ref> She was awarded a double [[master's degree]] in [[theoretical physics]] and [[mathematics]],<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.academia-net.org/profil/prof-anne-lhuillier/1135203|title=Prof. Anne L'huillier – AcademiaNet|website=www.academia-net.org|language=en|access-date=29 April 2017}}</ref> but switched for her [[doctorate degree]] to [[experimental physics]] at [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]].<ref name=''Wolf''>{{cite web|url=https://wolffund.org.il/2022/02/08/anne-lhuillier/|title=Anne L'Huillier|website=Wolf foundation|date=8 February 2022 |access-date=6 October 2023}}</ref> 
Her dissertation was on multiple multiphoton [[ionization]] in [[laser]] fields of high intensity. She carried out her dissertation research at the  [[Commissariat à l'énergie atomique et aux énergies alternatives]] (CEA), near Paris.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news|url=http://www.upmc.fr/en/university/history_and_famous_people/doctors_honoris_causa/dhc_2013/anne_l_huillier.html|title=Anne L'Huillier|last=UPMC|first=Université Pierre et Marie Curie -|date=12 December 2013|access-date=29 April 2017}}</ref>

=== Career ===
As a post-doctoral student, L'Huillier worked at the [[Chalmers Institute of Technology]] in [[Gothenburg]], Sweden, and at the [[University of Southern California ]] in [[Los Angeles]], United States.<ref name=":2"/> 
In 1986, L'Huillier obtained a permanent position as a researcher at the CEA, at the [[CEA Saclay|Saclay]] site.<ref name=":2"/>  

In 1992, she took part in an experiment in [[Lund]], where one of the first [[titanium]]-[[sapphire]] [[solid-state laser]] systems for [[femtosecond]] pulses in Europe had been installed. In 1994 she moved  to Sweden, where she was appointed at [[Lund University]] as a lecturer in 1995 and a professor in 1997.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.atomic.physics.lu.se/research/attosecond_physics/group_members/anne_lhuillier/|title=Anne L'Huillier|work=Atomic Physics, Faculty of Engineering, LTH|access-date=5 May 2014}}</ref> She also serves as governing board member at the [[Institut d'optique Graduate School|Institut d’optique]], France.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |date=8 November 2023 |title=Anne L'Huillier awarded a Doctor Honoris Causa from Université Paris-Saclay |url=http://www.universite-paris-saclay.fr/en/news/anne-lhuillier-awarded-doctor-honoris-causa-universite-paris-saclay |access-date=21 November 2023 |website=Université Paris-Saclay |language=en}}</ref>

== Research == 
L'Huillier's research involves experimental and theoretical aspects of [[high harmonic generation]] in gases, which corresponded to extremely short light pulses in the [[ultraviolet]] spectral range, lasting tens or hundreds of attoseconds. In 1987, L’Huillier first observed that gases like [[argon]] would react to a laser by becoming excited and emitting additional radiation or [[Overtone|overtones]], at various multiples of the frequency of laser.<ref name="Wood" />

In 1991, L'Huillier in collaboration with [[Kenneth J. Schafer|Kenneth Schafer]] and Kenneth Kulander presented numerical simulations of the time-dependent [[Schrödinger equation]] in order to understand the generation of high-order harmonics. They first  predicted the shape of the high harmonics spectrum and the [[phase-matching]] conditions.<ref name=":4">{{Cite journal |last=The Nobel Committee for Physics |date=3 October 2023 |title=Scientific Background to the Nobel Prize in Physics 2023 |url=https://www.nobelprize.org/uploads/2023/10/advanced-physicsprize2023.pdf |journal=The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences}}</ref> In 1994, [[Maciej Lewenstein]], L’Huiller and [[Paul Corkum]] presented a full [[Quantum mechanics|quantum theory]] of high harmonic generation.<ref name=":4" />
 
L'Huillier uses attosecond sources to study ultrafast dynamics of electrons in atomic and molecular systems.<ref name=":2" />  In 2003 her group beat the world record for the shortest laser pulse, lasting 170 [[attosecond]]s.<ref name="Fysik">{{Cite book |title=Fysik i Lund: i tid och rum |publisher=Fysiska institutionen i samarbete med Gidlunds förlag |year=2016 |isbn=9789178449729 |editor-last=Forkman |editor-first=Bengt |location=Lund |pages=371, 374 |language=sv |editor-last2=Holmin Verdozzi |editor-first2=Kristina}}</ref> These attosecond sources are considered the world's fastest cameras, using extremely short pulses of light to measure electrons as they move or change in energy.<ref name="Wood">{{cite news |last1=Wood |first1=Charlie |title=Physicists Who Explored Tiny Glimpses of Time Win Nobel Prize |url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/physicists-who-explored-tiny-glimpses-of-time-win-nobel-prize-20231003/ |work=Quanta magazine |date=3 October 2023}}</ref><ref name="Pollard">{{cite news |last1=Pollard |first1=Niklas |last2=Ahlander |first2=Johan |title=Nobel physics prize goes to trio who lit up secrets of the atom |url=https://www.reuters.com/science/agostini-krausz-lhuillier-win-2023-nobel-prize-physics-2023-10-03/ |work=Reuters |date=3 October 2023 |language=en}}</ref> L’Huillier's methods for studying and manipulating electrons using light have pioneered the field of attochemistry as they allow the study electronic processes during chemical reactions.<ref name="Wood" />

In 2010,  an experiment led by [[Ferenc Krausz]] at the [[Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics]], highlighted a discrepancy between theory and experimental results concerning [[Photoelectric effect|photoemission]] delays in [[neon]] atoms. L'Huillier group in Lund solved this problem in 2017 by experimentally uncovering the contribution of [[Radiative Auger effect|shake-up electrons]]. By correcting for this effect L'Huillier group found an excellent agreement with theory.<ref name=":4" />

== Honors and awards ==
L'Huillier was on the [[Nobel Committee for Physics]] between 2007 and 2015,<ref name=":0" /> and has been a member of the [[Swedish Academy of Sciences]] since 2004.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.kva.se/sv/nyheter/nya-ledamoter-2|title=Nya ledamöter|date=19 April 2004|website=Kungl. Vetenskapsakademien|access-date=29 April 2017}}</ref> In 2003, she received the {{ill|Julius Springer Prize|de|Julius-Springer-Preis für angewandte Physik}}. In 2011 she received a [[UNESCO L'Oréal Award]]. In 2013, she was awarded the {{Interlanguage link|Carl-Zeiss Research Award|de}}, the {{ill|Blaise Pascal Medal|de|Blaise-Pascal-Medaille|pt|Medalha Blaise Pascal}} and an Honorary Degree at [[Université Pierre et Marie Curie]] (UPMC), Paris.<ref name=":1" /> She was elected a foreign associate of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2018. One year later, in 2019, she was recognized with the Prize for Fundamental Aspects of Quantum Electronics and Optics, announced by the [[European Physical Society]]. Anne L'Huillier is a fellow member of the [[American Physical Society]] and [[Optica (society)|Optica]].<ref>{{cite news |title=EPS Quantum Electronics Prizes |url=http://qeod.epsdivisions.org/QEOD%20Prizes/eps-quantum-electronics-prize |access-date=13 June 2020 |archive-date=5 May 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160505062134/http://qeod.epsdivisions.org/QEOD%20Prizes/eps-quantum-electronics-prize |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2021 L'Huillier was awarded the [[The Optical Society|Optical Society of America]] Max Born Award for "pioneering work in ultrafast laser science and attosecond physics, realizing and understanding high harmonic generation and applying it to time-resolved imaging of electron motion in atoms and molecules".<ref>{{Cite web|title=Max Born Award|url=https://www.osa.org/en-us/awards_and_grants/awards/award_description/maxborn/#:~:text=Presented%20to%20an%20individual%20who,general%20and%20optics%20in%20particular.|url-status=live|website=OSA|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131014050519/http://www.osa.org/en-us/awards_and_grants/awards/award_description/maxborn/ |archive-date=14 October 2013 }}</ref> In 2022 she received the [[Wolf Prize in Physics]] for "pioneering contributions to ultrafast laser science and attosecond physics" jointly with [[Ferenc Krausz]] and [[Paul Corkum]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=8 February 2022 |title=Anne L'Huillier |url=https://wolffund.org.il/2022/02/08/anne-lhuillier/ |access-date=6 October 2023 |website=Wolf Foundation |language=en-US}}</ref> Also for 2022, the three were awarded the [[BBVA Foundation Frontiers of Knowledge Award]] in Basic Sciences.<ref>{{Cite web |date=22 February 2023 |title=The Frontiers of Knowledge Award goes to Anne L'Huillier, Paul Corkum and Ferenc Krausz for enabling subatomic particles to be observed in motion over the shortest time scale captured by science |url=https://www.frontiersofknowledgeawards-fbbva.es/noticias/15th-edition-basic-sciences-anne-lhuillier-paul-corkum-ferenc-krausz/ |access-date=6 October 2023 |website=Premios Fronteras |language=en}}</ref> She also received the French [[Legion of Honour]] the same year.<ref>{{Citation |title=Décret du 29 décembre 2022 portant promotion et nomination dans l'ordre national de la Légion d'honneur |url=https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/jorf/id/JORFTEXT000046850463 |access-date=12 October 2023}}</ref>

In September 2023, she received the [[Berthold Leibinger Zukunftspreis]] for "high harmonic generation and attosecond physics'''."'''<ref>{{Cite web |title=Berthold Leibinger Preisverleihung |url=https://photonicsbw.de/news/detail/berthold-leibinger-preisverleihung-2853/ |access-date=12 October 2023 |website=photonicsbw.de |language=de}}</ref> In October 2023, she was awarded the [[Nobel Prize in Physics]], jointly with Krausz and  [[Pierre Agostini]] "for experimental methods that generate attosecond pulses of light for the study of electron dynamics in matter".<ref name="davis-2023" />

In November 2023, she received a [[Honorary degree|doctor honoris causa]] from [[Paris-Saclay University]]. During the ceremony, 2022 Nobel Prize in Physics, [[Alain Aspect]] was the guest of honor.<ref name=":5" />

In March 2024, she received a doctor honoris causa from [[University of Bordeaux]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=29 March 2024 |title=Anne L'Huillier (Lund University) |url=https://www.u-bordeaux.fr/en/about-us/honoris-causa/anne-lhuillier-lund-university |access-date=13 April 2024 |website=University of Bordeaux |language=en}}</ref> and in May from the [[University of Porto]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Silva |first=Renata |date=24 May 2024 |title=Anne L'Huillier será a próxima Doutora Honoris Causa da U.Porto |url=https://noticias.up.pt/2024/05/24/anne-lhuillier-sera-a-proxima-doutora-honoris-causa-da-u-porto/ |access-date=7 June 2024 |website=Notícias U.Porto |language=pt-PT}}</ref>

In September 2024, she was awarded the Great Gold Medal by the Royal Swedish Academy of Engineering Sciences (IVA), the society's highest honor.<ref>{{Cite web |title=IVA's Great Gold Medal 2024: Anne L'Huillier – opened the door to the world of atoms |url=https://www.iva.se/en/published/ivas-great-gold-medal-2024-anne-lhuillier--opened-the-door-to-the-world-of-atoms/ |access-date=2026-11-07 |website=www.iva.se |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
L'Huillier is married to {{ill|Claes-Göran Wahlström|sv}} who is also a professor at Lund University.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Svanberg |first=Sune |date=4 October 2023 |title=How we hired 2023 Nobel laureate Anne L'Huillier – and why we knew she was destined for greatness |url=http://theconversation.com/how-we-hired-2023-nobel-laureate-anne-lhuillier-and-why-we-knew-she-was-destined-for-greatness-214867 |access-date=5 October 2023 |website=The Conversation |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Conrad |first1=Lina |title=Glädjekaos runt L'Huillier: "Kan inte komma i närheten" |url=https://sverigesradio.se/artikel/kaos-runt-lhuillier-kan-inte-komma-i-narheten |access-date=3 January 2024 |date=3 October 2023 |language=Swedish}}</ref> They have two children.<ref>{{cite web | title=Anne L'Huillier awarded Nobel Prize in Physics | website=Lund University | date=4 October 2023 | url=https://www.lunduniversity.lu.se/article/anne-lhuillier-awarded-nobel-prize-physics | access-date=28 June 2024}}</ref><ref name="autobiographical">{{cite web | title=The Nobel Prize in Physics 2023 |last=L'Huillier | first=Anne | website=NobelPrize.org | date=28 June 2024 | url=https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2023/lhuillier/biographical/ | access-date=28 June 2024}}</ref>
